Definition: a petition; by implication, a loan
BiblicalUsage: A petition is something asked for, and sometimes something lent. Bathsheba comes to Solomon with one petition and asks him not to deny her, Esther hears the king ask what is thy petition, and it shall be granted thee, and Gideon asks a request of the men of Israel. In Samuel the same word is a loan: Eli blesses Elkanah for the loan which is lent to the LORD, the child Hannah gave back to God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe petitions show us how God wants to be approached: boldly, plainly, and with the expectation that He hears. Hannah asked and gave back; Esther asked and was granted; and I hold that asking is not weakness but faith.
